name: Yantai Penglai International Airport
before:
Yantai's airport, 43 km from the city centre in Penglai District, which is a long way out and worth factoring into a transfer.

It is new. Construction started in December 2009 and the airport opened on 28 May 2015, when every flight serving Yantai transferred over from the old Laishan Airport. The first arrival was a China Eastern service from Beijing that landed five minutes after midnight.

It has not grown as fast as planned. The 80,000 square metre terminal and 3,400 metre runway were built for 12 million passengers and 90,000 tonnes of cargo a year by 2020, but the airport handled 8,036,554 passengers and 72,622 tonnes in 2025, well short of those projections. In practical terms that means it is not congested.

Skytrax rates it three stars.

It was originally called Yantai Chaoshui International and took its current name in April 2014.
after:
Yantai's airport, 43 km from the city centre, which is a long way out and worth factoring into a transfer.

It is new. The airport opened on 28 May 2015, when every flight serving Yantai transferred over from the old Laishan Airport.

Terminal 2 opened in 2024, and the airport says it can handle 23 million passengers and 200,000 tonnes of cargo a year. Traffic in 2025 was 8,036,554 passengers and 72,622 tonnes, well short of that. In practical terms that means it is not congested.

claims.note: CAAC: 8,036,554 passengers (down 6.9 per cent on 2024) and 72,622.4 tonnes of cargo and mail (down 7 per cent). 'Well short of that' compares these with the operator's stated capacity: about a third of the passenger figure.

sources.quote: in 2025, the actual number of passenger movements was only 8,036,554 while the actual cargo movements were 72,622.4 tons

claims.why: Sources disagree on the district: Wikipedia puts the airport near Chaoshui in Penglai District, while the operator's own postal address puts its office in Chaoshui town under the Yantai Development Zone (烟台市开发区潮水镇). The distance is kept.
Wikipedia alone; the operator's history does not record it and the 2014 Yantai government report only calls it the new airport.

claims.claim: not grown as fast as planned
claims.wasBefore: It has not grown as fast as planned.
claims.why: Rests on the 2020 projection, which is Wikipedia's alone. The comparison the text now makes is with the operator's stated capacity.

claims.claim: 80,000 square metre terminal and 3,400 m runway built for 12 million and 90,000 tonnes by 2020
claims.wasBefore: The 80,000 square metre terminal and 3,400 metre runway were built for 12 million passengers and 90,000 tonnes of cargo a year by 2020
claims.why: Out of date: it described the 2015 terminal, and Terminal 2 has been in use since 2024 (operator; Yantai government). The 80,000 square metres and the 2020 projections rest on Wikipedia alone. The runway's 3,400 m is confirmed by OurAirports but is left out as it no longer carries the point.
The projections are cut; the comparison is now with the operator's stated capacity ('well short of that').

Skytrax's live page still shows a 3-Star Domestic Airport rating, but its assessment is of Terminal 1 and says 'A new Terminal 2 is being built'. Passengers have used Terminal 2 since 2024, so the rating describes the old building.

claims.why: Wikipedia alone. Its source, a NetEase report of April 2014, now answers 404, and the Yantai government's 2014 work report calls it only the new airport.
